column2: The ground floor elevator lobby of a brand new glass skyscraper on the far west side of Manhattan, looking straight down the lobby toward a bank of six tall brushed steel elevator doors at the far end, polished white terrazzo floor, a huge black building directory board on the right wall listing floors in white letters, warm downlights in a slatted oak ceiling, floor to ceiling glass on the left showing a rainy evening street with a yellow cab, a security desk with a guard, a few people in hoodies and sneakers waiting for the lift, a giant hand drawn doodle mural of a cloud over a mound of dirt on the back wall.

The basement stockroom of a big suburban New Jersey wine and liquor store in 1994, looking straight down a long aisle between towering metal shelves of cardboard wine cases and stacked crates, a bare fluorescent tube ceiling, a concrete floor, a folding table far down the aisle piled with baseball cards in plastic sleeves, a beige 1990s computer with a bulky monitor glowing on a desk, a price gun, a dolly, hand written cardboard signs, one teenager in a hoodie restocking a shelf far away.

The set of a scrappy 2006 internet wine show, looking straight at a cheap desk in front of a wall of wooden wine racks: on the desk a row of open wine bottles, a big silver spit bucket, a mess of tasting glasses, a green football helmet as a prop, a flip calendar, a camcorder on a tripod to the side, a green team pennant, a dusty window, harsh video lights, a wall of VHS tapes and a whiteboard that says EPISODE 1000, no person at the desk.

A boxing gym inside an old Manhattan loft with a vast wall of bookshelves: looking straight down the gym past a boxing ring with red ropes toward a row of heavy bags hanging from the ceiling, tall arched windows, wooden floorboards, giant books the size of doors leaning against the walls with blank spines, a chalkboard that says JAB JAB JAB, old fight posters with flower headed boxers, a few boxers training far away.

The open plan office floor of a large creative advertising agency on a high floor of a Manhattan skyscraper on the far west side, looking straight across the floor to a wall of floor to ceiling windows with a sweeping view of the Hudson River, the sunset, and the rooftops of Chelsea far below, long white desks with monitors, exposed black ceiling with ducts, a glass box content studio with a ring light and a phone on a tripod, whiteboards covered in doodles and sticky notes, a neon sign that says VEE, young people in hoodies and sneakers working far away.

A podcast and video studio with black walls and warm neon, looking straight at a long dark wooden desk with three broadcast microphones on arms, two leather chairs, a wall of 64 smartphones on a grid stand all glowing with vertical videos, three cinema cameras on tripods, a red ON AIR lamp, acoustic foam panels, LED tube lights in pink and blue, a neon sign reading CLOUDS AND DIRT, nobody at the desk.

Park Avenue in Manhattan at dusk, looking straight up the avenue from the middle of the grassy centre median with tulips and small trees, the grand limestone apartment buildings on both sides with lit windows, doormen under green awnings, the avenue running away to the distant tower that straddles the street, soft purple blue sky, a few people with flower heads walking dogs far away, the pavement wet from rain.

The historic carousel in Central Park at twilight inside its brick pavilion with open arches, looking straight at the carousel from the pavilion floor: dozens of hand painted wooden horses mid gallop under a canopy of warm bulbs and mirrored panels, a brass ring post, a ticket booth, the park trees and lamps glowing outside the arches, a single black cat sitting on one of the horses, a few flower headed children and parents waiting by the rail far back.

Standing on the stage of a huge sold out indoor arena at night looking straight out at the crowd: ten thousand people with flower heads under a storm of pink and blue stage light, confetti falling, phones held up, giant LED screens on both sides showing a cartoon cloud and a mound of dirt, a catwalk running out into the crowd, haze, the ceiling rigging and spotlights, an arena sign that says VEE.

The floor of a frantic stock exchange reimagined as an attention exchange, looking straight down the floor: a wall of giant screens showing jagged green and red line charts labelled only with short words like SHORT VIDEO, PODCAST, NEWSLETTER, LIVE, STREET, dozens of traders with flower heads in coloured jackets shouting and waving tickets, scrolling LED ticker tape bands with numbers, paper on the floor, a big central board that says ATTENTION, brass railings.

Looking out from the open front of a luxury owner's suite high in a modern football stadium at night onto the field below: the green field with white yard lines and tall yellow goal posts, a packed crowd in green and white, floodlights, the suite's leather seats and marble bar in the foreground sides, a green banner that says N3W, steam of breath in cold air, confetti, a jumbotron showing a cartoon cloud.

Standing on an open rooftop observation deck above the clouds at sunrise, looking straight out over a sea of golden pink clouds with the tops of the Manhattan skyscrapers poking through, the Empire State Building spire and the tallest downtown tower lit by the first sun, a glass railing far ahead, a wooden deck, a single white bench, a weather vane, birds, the sky huge and clear above.
